capability_gaps.mods: Claude Code function hooks have no Codex equivalent. Codex never sees the `modules` key: since 5.0.0 its manifest points `hooks` at the generated Codex hooks file, and since 5.0.2 the key lives in the mod's own hooks file, which only the Claude manifest's `hooks` field names, so the settings hooks file carries no mod reference on any host.
capability_gaps.slash_commands: No plugin-shippable command mechanism found. All 9 plugins bundled with codex 0.156.0 (browser, chrome, codex-app-tools, computer-use, latex, messages, record-and-replay, unified-computer-use, visualize) were checked: 0 declare a commands manifest field and 0 ship a commands/ directory. Codex publishes no manifest reference to cite, so this is the strongest available evidence rather than a documented absence - it means a plugin cannot CONTRIBUTE commands, not that Codex has no built-in ones. The adjacent surface Codex does offer is interface.defaultPrompt, which this plugin ships with 6 entries as of 4.5.0.

One upstream change touches the generated policies and was checked: 0.70.0 evaluates policy `argsPattern`/`commandRegex` with RE2 (re2js; no lookaround, backreferences or \uXXXX; google-gemini/gemini-cli#30282) and wraps `commandRegex` as `\x00"command":"(?:...)` so it matches only the top-level command argument (#30355). The four rules in platforms/gemini/policies/tamirs-superpowers.toml use none of the removed syntax and have no top-level alternation; compiled with re2js 2.9.0 in that wrapped form and matched against stableStringify-shaped arguments, each compiles and matches as intended (force-push and `-f` denied, --force-with-lease not; `branch -D` denied, `-d` not; lockfiles and .yarn/releases denied, src/index.ts not). The three upstream docs this adapter is written against were diffed between the v0.60.0 and v0.62.0 tags - docs/extensions/reference.md, docs/cli/skills.md, docs/core/subagents.md - and are byte-identical, so gemini-extension.json, the generated flat skill mirror and the subagent adapter need no change. 0.61.0: security fixes (indirect prompt injection via build-file modifications and untrusted flags; hardened sandbox filesystem boundaries and isolated runtime state), explicit versioned Flash model ids preserved, AgentLoopContext properties preserved across spreads - host-side hardening, nothing to adopt. 0.62.0: MCP tool-call titles formatted as structured signatures with explanations segregated (cosmetic for this repo's MCP stubs); OAuth refresh token retained on refresh and idempotent credential deletion; ACP mode emits tool_call before request_permission; ConPTY/PTY lifecycle and Windows terminal-buffer fixes; Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.5 Flash Lite added (no model pinned here). No extension, skill, subagent, hook, settings or headless-flag change in the range; no breaking change affects this repo. Install pinning and headless mode (2026-09-23, live on gemini 0.60.0): `gemini extensions install --help` and `gemini skills install --help` confirm --ref (any git ref), --auto-update and --pre-release; `gemini --help` confirms -p/--prompt for non-interactive mode, -o/--output-format with text|json|stream-json, and --approval-mode with default|auto_edit|yolo|plan. Flag surfaces read off the live 0.60.0 binary, not the docs. No prompt was executed, so this records the flags as available rather than the headless path as exercised end to end; validated_against is unchanged. live run on 2026-09-23 against Gemini CLI 0.60.0, upgraded from 0.55.1 via `npm i -g @google/gemini-cli`. First direct CLI validation on this row since 0.55.1, which it replaces, closing the five-minor gap in which 0.57-0.60 hardened symlink resolution, extension-loader paths, workspace boundaries and env-var sanitization — the four mechanisms this adapter is built on. CONFIRMED: `gemini extensions validate .` reports 'Extension . has been successfully validated'; the `gemini skills` subcommand surface the install guide depends on (list/enable/disable/install/link) is intact, unlike OpenCode v2 which removed its equivalent; and the generated flat mirror at .gemini/skills/ holds 29 symlinks, all 29 resolving to a real SKILL.md with 0 broken — the specific thing the symlink-resolution hardening could have broken. NOT confirmed by CLI listing: project skill discovery, because `gemini skills list --all` reports 'Skipping project agents due to untrusted folder' in this checkout, a workspace-trust condition rather than an adapter defect.

capability_gaps.dynamic_workflows: The Workflow tool is Claude-specific; no declared Gemini equivalent.
capability_gaps.mods: No equivalent; the Gemini extension reads no hooks file from this repo.
capability_gaps.parallel_subagents: Gemini subagents cannot themselves call subagents — documented recursion protection, not merely unmeasured. orchestrate-dev's fan-out pattern is structurally impossible on Gemini as a result.

capability_source_note: targets.<key>.capabilities and capability_gaps are DERIVED from the capability registry and must not be hand-edited. Regenerate with `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --sync-capabilities`; `scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh` fails when they drift.
version_claims_note: `validated_against` is the version this repo was last exercised against on a live maintainer machine. `reviewed_through` is the newest upstream release whose notes have actually been read for adapter impact. They are different claims and they drift apart on purpose: reading release notes is cheap and should always be current, while a live run needs a maintainer at a machine. V1-04 fires on `reviewed_through < latest_known` -- nobody has looked at what shipped -- because that is the gap a contributor can actually close. It deliberately does not fire on a validated_against lag, which is bounded instead by `last_reviewed` and V1-05's 90-day budget. A target with no `reviewed_through` falls back to `validated_against`, so consumer repos that have not adopted the field score exactly as before.
